observation.visible_scene: A large faceted crystal/glass sphere with an internal crackle structure that shows iridescent rainbow colors, resting on a small metallic pedestal. The pedestal has a lower cylindrical base and an upper disc from which three short vertical prongs rise to cradle the sphere's lower edge. The object sits on a pale circular tabletop against a plain neutral gray wall.
visible_changes: The sphere's center stays at roughly the same image position throughout, while the three support prongs shift horizontally around its lower rim (the left prong stays near the left, the middle prong moves leftward, the right prong moves leftward), indicating the sphere-and-holder assembly rotates about a vertical axis.
The internal faceted pattern and the bright rainbow highlights continuously reorganize and sweep across the sphere's volume, consistent with that rotation changing which facets face the camera.
The dark reflective crescents on the left and right sides of the sphere change size and position over time as the surface rotates relative to the fixed environment reflections.
The lower metal base, the gray background, and the tabletop edge remain essentially fixed, so the apparent motion is object rotation rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What drives the rotation (motorized turntable vs. manual) and whether the rotation was already ongoing before the crop and continues after it.
The exact orientation of the holder prongs relative to the sphere at the start and end of the segment.
Whether the lighting or a polarizing filter is also changing.
uncertain_details: The precise rotation direction and angular speed cannot be measured from these sparse samples; only the relative leftward drift of the two right-side prongs and the changing facet pattern are clearly supported.
Small residual camera motion cannot be fully excluded, but background and base evidence suggests the camera is static.
It is not certain whether the dark lobes are reflections of the room or actual dark facets of the object.
